sections.heading: When to use
sections.text: Use PSFB for 200W-5kW isolated applications requiring high efficiency. Phase-shift modulation between the two legs achieves ZVS on primary switches. Power transfer: Vout = Vin*(2*D-1)/N where D is the effective duty cycle of overlapping conduction.

sections.heading: Controller structure
sections.text: Use current-mode control with slope compensation for the extended duty range. The phase-shift between legs is the primary control variable. Current sensing on the primary with a current transformer or sense resistor.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: Duty-cycle loss: the effective duty cycle at the secondary is less than the primary due to the phase-shift overlap. ZVS is maintained by the transformer leakage inductance and MOSFET output capacitance. At light load, ZVS may be lost.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If PSFB efficiency is below target at light load, ZVS is likely lost. Options: (1) add a saturable inductor to extend ZVS range, (2) use adaptive dead-time control, (3) accept the switching loss if the load range is narrow.
